function.arguments: {"observation": "`patient_id` has 48 duplicate values — rows may not be one-per-entity", "implication": "The `patient_id` column is not unique, meaning some patients appear more than once in the dataset. According to the data dictionary, this is because some patients were re-tested, and both rows are present. The data dictionary explicitly states that the row with the highest `sample_seq` supersedes earlier rows for that patient. Therefore, to compute the mean across all patients (not rows), we must deduplicate the data by `patient_id`, keeping the row with the highest `sample_seq`. Failure to do so would double-weight the re-tested patients, biasing the mean upward."}
function.name: note_finding
